heading: Models compute features for later tokens beyond immediate next-token prediction
definition: models compute features at one position because they help later positions, not only as a side effect of predicting the next token (breadcrumbs).
summary: Independent studies reproduce a qualitative signature of this mechanism through myopic-training comparisons in small models. Larger-model evidence shows later use of intermediate information without establishing its training origin.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy/<1B: R2 for the qualitative myopic-training signature, with quantitative results in arXiv:2603.14087#R5, arXiv:2603.14087#R6 and arXiv:2603.14087#R10; the informal study reports minimal performance reduction at 117M and increasing cost with scale (lw:c68SJsBpiAxkPwRHj#R1, lw:c68SJsBpiAxkPwRHj#R2). 1-10B: R0 for each distinct setting: Gemma 2 2B final-checkpoint SAE-ablation estimates (arXiv:2603.14087#R15), and informal myopic-training results extending to 1.5B without quantitative performance results (lw:c68SJsBpiAxkPwRHj#R2). 10-100B: R0 for indirect evidence from Qwen-72B operator-token probes; the attention bridge routes first-addend information without isolating a computed sum (arXiv:2407.11421#R1, arXiv:2407.11421#R2, arXiv:2407.11421#R11). >100B: R0 for DeepSeek V3 filler-position causal KV-cache results and DeepSeek V3/Kimi K2 decoding; training incentives remain untested (arXiv:2607.03502#r1, arXiv:2607.03502#r15, arXiv:2607.03502#r21).
suggested_status.reason: counts: versions.V3.studies_tested = 4; versions.V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0; versions.V3.verdicts.challenges.studies = 0; versions.V3.original_sources_linked = []. R2 rests on the qualitative myopic-training signature reported in arXiv:2603.14087#R5, arXiv:2603.14087#R6 and arXiv:2603.14087#R10 and informally in lw:c68SJsBpiAxkPwRHj#R2, with different settings and evidence strength. The informal study spans 117M–1.5B, reports minimal cost at 117M and increasing cost with scale, and supplies no quantitative performance results (lw:c68SJsBpiAxkPwRHj#R1, lw:c68SJsBpiAxkPwRHj#R2). Thus counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size, whose keys are '<1B' and 'not stated', understates the reported size coverage. Qwen-72B intermediate-sum decodability depends on layer, operator position and task prompt; reduced later-layer resolution at the fourth and fifth '+' limits this result. Its bridge intervention routes operand information and does not establish causal use of a computed sum or its training origin (arXiv:2407.11421#R1, arXiv:2407.11421#R2, arXiv:2407.11421#R3, arXiv:2407.11421#R4, arXiv:2407.11421#R11, arXiv:2407.11421#R22, arXiv:2407.11421#R23). DeepSeek V3 filler-position KV transplants establish causal later use in the tested arithmetic settings, without manipulating training incentives (arXiv:2607.03502#r15, arXiv:2607.03502#r16, arXiv:2607.03502#r17, arXiv:2607.03502#r18). Gemma readout-alignment correlations do not establish absence of pre-caching and supply no V3 scope-limit verdict (arXiv:2603.14087#R17, arXiv:2603.14087#R18, arXiv:2603.14087#R19, arXiv:2603.14087#R20, arXiv:2603.14087#R21). The remaining scope limits still support counts: versions.V3.studies_with_limits_scope = 4. With no original linked to V3, reproduction is assessed against the version statement.
suggested_status.open_questions: Would a quantitative myopic-training or gradient-decomposition test on a pretrained LM of at least 1B, or an independent repetition of filler-position KV transplants on another family, raise the larger-scale levels? Can a direct intervention establish later use of Qwen's decoded intermediate sums, beyond operand-information routing (arXiv:2407.11421#R11)? Would matched training conditions reconcile minimal cost at 117M (lw:c68SJsBpiAxkPwRHj#R1) with the TinyStories myopic-training loss increase (arXiv:2603.14087#R10)? A matched failed replication could change the small-scale level to C. Would tests in verse or planning tasks connect V3 to V1/V4?

source.title: Tracing the Thoughts of a Large Language Model

original_result.result: No original study is identified for this claim.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Qwen-72B represented running sums at positions where they could not aid next-token prediction.
Filler positions carried intermediate computations that causally influenced later answers.
Blocking training signals from future positions increasingly hurt performance as GPT-2-style models grew.
Transformers learned features with delayed benefits, and myopic training impaired performance.
Running-sum decoding weakened at later operator positions.
DeepSeek V3 weakly represented parallel addends, and second-addend transplants rarely swapped answers completely.
Enforced myopia barely reduced performance in the 117M model.
Syntax features survived myopic training and relied more on direct than delayed influence.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: The training-incentive part ('because they help later positions') in pretrained LMs above toy scale. Myopic training appears only in models trained from scratch. The large-model studies (Qwen-72B; DeepSeek V3, Kimi K2) do not test whether the computation arises because training rewards later use.

Untested-parts lines of arXiv:2607.03502 ('Does not test whether the filler computation arises because training rewards later use') and arXiv:2407.11421 ('No myopic-training or breadcrumbs-vs-pre-caching comparison').

untested.what: Pre-caching in verse, rhyme or planning tasks (the setting of V1/V4).
untested.basis: Untested-parts line of arXiv:2603.14087 ('Pre-caching is not tested in verse or planning tasks'). The other studies use synthetic arithmetic, toy tasks, TinyStories or inserted filler.

untested.what: Pre-cached influence over the course of training in a pretrained LLM: Gemma 2 2B Q(w) is estimated only near the final checkpoint.
Causal intervention on the intermediate-sum state itself in iterative arithmetic. The attention-mask test routes addend information, not a sum.

Fine-tuned models, the Llama and Mistral families, and reasoning-trained models with explicit reasoning enabled. Kimi K2.5 has direct intermediate-decoding and behavioral results with explicit reasoning suppressed by an empty think block.

untested.what: Which earlier-position features serve later tokens in the myopia experiments up to 1.5B: there is only an aggregate performance gap, with no feature-level evidence or intervention.

wording_issues.issue: Training incentives are tested through myopic training of models trained from scratch (toy tasks and TinyStories in arXiv:2603.14087; GPT-2-style models spanning 117M–1.5B, without quantitative performance results, in lw:c68SJsBpiAxkPwRHj) and gradient decomposition (arXiv:2603.14087 R8, R14). In DeepSeek V3, arXiv:2607.03502 measures filler-position intermediate decoding and causal later use through KV-cache transplants, without a training-incentive manipulation or myopic-training comparison. In Qwen-72B, arXiv:2407.11421 decodes intermediate sums at operator tokens; its attention bridge routes first-addend information without isolating causal use of a computed sum. It reports no myopic-training or gradient-decomposition comparison. These experimental designs leave training incentives untested in the large models; this is not an explicit training-reward disclaimer from either paper.

The share of pre-caching depends on the feature. POS and dependency features show no myopic/non-myopic probe difference, and direct influence exceeds pre-cached influence in all layers (R12, R13). A positional feature has pre-cached influence above direct influence only in layers 2–3 (R14). In Gemma 2 2B, features with heavy delayed-influence tails are concentrated in formal domains (σ 1.63 ± 0.03 vs 1.23 ± 0.02; R15).

wording_issues.phrase: not only as a side effect of predicting the next token (breadcrumbs)
wording_issues.issue: In Qwen-72B, early-layer probe maxima for intermediate sums persist under the ignore-formula prompt, while later-layer accuracies decrease (R22, R23). This does not separate next-token from later-position training incentives or identify the early-layer sums as breadcrumbs. In GPT-2-style models trained from scratch, the myopia cost is described as minimal at 117M, without quantitative performance results (lw R1). The statement does not specify the relative contribution of pre-caching or where it applies.

The measured later use is often partial. Filler-region KV transplants on DeepSeek V3 shift donor rank, but full answer swaps are 7.4% (A1) and 2.8% (A2) on 2-fact addition, and the system-of-equations effect is mostly corruption rather than clean swaps (r16–r18). In Qwen-72B iterative addition with 2–10 numbers, the attention bridge masks subsequent tokens' direct attention to the first addend while allowing access through the first '+'. Exact-answer accuracy remains non-trivial but drops significantly relative to baseline (figure only; R11–R19). The bridge routes first-addend information without isolating a computed intermediate-sum state, so this result cannot determine V3's pre-caching mechanism or independently establish a V3 scope limit.

method_sensitivity.what: The cost of enforced myopia is described as minimal at 117M and growing with scale up to 1.5B (informal, no numbers).

Pre-cached against direct influence differs by feature. In TinyStories, the positional feature has pre-cached influence above direct influence (layers 2–3), while POS and dependency features have direct influence above pre-cached influence in all layers. In Gemma 2 2B, formal-domain features have σ 1.63 ± 0.03 against 1.23 ± 0.02 for non-formal features.

The positional feature's pre-cached influence exceeds direct influence only in layers 2–3, not layer 1 (verdict fix on R14). In Qwen-72B, the ignore-formula prompt leaves first-ten-layer sum probes unaffected but significantly lowers later-layer accuracy.

In Qwen-72B iterative addition, a prompt telling the model to ignore the formula leaves maximum first-ten-layer sum-probe accuracies unaffected while significantly reducing later-layer accuracies. Training incentives and causal dependence on later use are not tested.

Qwen-72B sum probes work at the 2nd–3rd '+' (R1, R2), with later-layer maxima of 74% at the fourth '+' and 62% at the fifth '+'. The final '=' has a later-layer maximum of 37%, but this is cannot_determine for V3 because the sum is relevant to the next output token. In DeepSeek V3 KV transplants, addend-decoded filler positions carry 85-93% of the effect and complement positions carry little (verdict reason).
On 2-fact addition with dots and counting filler, both addends are in the top-2 decoded tokens in 35.2% on DeepSeek V3 against 74.1% on Kimi K2.

The record's method-sensitivity line says scrambled filler underperforms, very long filler can asymptote or degrade, filler placed before the question gives no behavioural uplift, and residual subtraction helps only in some settings. Decoding is aggregated over nine filler conditions (dots, alphabet, counting; k = 5–100) for 1-fact addition.

For Gemma 2 2B readouts targeting two and three tokens ahead, pre-cached influence has a small negative Spearman correlation with look-ahead readout alignment; Pearson correlations are near zero. These correlations support the V6 breadcrumbs interpretation but are cannot_determine for V3's training-incentive claim. They do not establish a V3 scope limit or the absence of features learned for later use.

In Qwen-72B iterative addition with 2–10 numbers, an attention mask blocks subsequent tokens from attending directly to the first addend while allowing access through the first '+'. Exact-answer accuracy remains non-trivial but drops significantly from baseline (figure only). The intervention demonstrates routing of first-addend information without isolating a computed intermediate sum; R11–R19 are cannot_determine for V3.
